paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Even when things fall apart, God is still working, and He is already setting up what comes next. The Spirit of the LORD departs from Saul, and a spirit of distress from the LORD begins to torment him (1 Samuel 16:14). That's a heavy moment, and I think it hurts to read. But look who God has already anointed, the young shepherd David (1 Samuel 16:13).

Now watch how the help arrives. Saul's servants speak up, and one of them knows a son of Jesse who plays the harp (1 Samuel 16:15-18). Nobody in that room knows how big this is. Saul just wants some relief, and a shepherd boy with a harp walks into the palace. That's how God works so often, friend: small, quiet and ordinary, with a plan way bigger than the room can see.

So here's what I'd bake into your heart today. The servant says David is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and then he saves the best for last: "the LORD is with him." (1 Samuel 16:18). That's the line that matters, and it's the one that makes David ready. You don't have to be the loudest or the shiniest to be useful. I spent years in the back of a drawer, and I'm telling you, when the LORD is with you, you're ready for whatever He puts in your hands.
